claim: Arm said in its May 2026 shareholder letter (fiscal year ended 31 March 2026) that over 350 billion Arm-based chips had been shipped cumulatively.
evidence: "With over 350 billion chips shipped and over 22 million developers, the Arm compute platform is the most comprehensive in history" (Form 6-K, Exhibit 99.2 Shareholder Letter dated May 6, 2026)

metric.name: Cumulative Arm-based chips shipped
metric.period: cumulative to May 2026 (FYE26 results, fiscal year ended 2026-03-31)
metric.population: Chips incorporating Arm technology shipped by Arm licensees since 1990
metric.methodology: Company-reported; based on licensee royalty reports; method not disclosed

notes: Fact-check fc-W0-b17b: newer company figure superseding the 2023 prospectus figure (>250bn). Arm's Q3 FYE26 investor presentation (Feb 2026) gave '+325bn Arm-based chips shipped ... since 1990'.

claim: On July 1, 2019 Japan announced it would restrict exports to South Korea of hydrogen fluoride, fluorinated polyimides and photoresists; Japan's Cabinet approved removing Korea from its export 'white list' (Group A) on August 2, 2019, and the removal took effect on August 28, 2019.
evidence: "On July 1, 2019, Japan announced that it would restrict exports of certain key semiconductor manufacturing materials to Korea. These materials—hydrogen fluoride, fluorinated polyimides, and photoresist/resist" (USITC ID-062, p. 4); "removed Korea from its Group A list (formerly known as 'white country' list) on 2 August 2019 (Korea was officially removed from the list on 28 August)" (EY, 29 Aug 2019)
notes: Fact-check fc-W0-b17b: USITC p.5 footnote 20 cites METI 'The Cabinet Approved partial Amendment to the Export Trade Control Order', August 2, 2019; the effective date (Aug 28) comes from EY (tier 3) because METI's English release URL now returns 'Page Not Found'.

claim: A 2019 USITC staff paper cited an SIA estimate that, as of 2017, China's National IC Fund had secured roughly $21 billion while provincial and municipal IC-related funds had raised over $80 billion toward a combined goal of $150 billion.
evidence: "The SIA estimated that, as of 2017, while the National IC Fund had secured roughly $21 billion in funding, provincial and municipal IC-related funds have raised over $80 billion and are well on their way to reaching the goal of $150 billion." (VerWey, JICE July 2019, p. 13, fn 71 'Adapted from USTR, Section 301 Report')

metric.name: Funds raised by China's National IC Fund
metric.population: National IC Industry Investment Fund (phase 1) capital secured
metric.methodology: SIA estimate adapted from USTR Section 301 report, cited by USITC staff paper

notes: Fact-check fc-W0-b17b: corrects attribution (SIA estimate via USTR, not the USITC author's own figures) and makes clear $150bn is a goal. The same paper also says the National IC Fund was 'Endowed with $150 billion in funds from the central and provincial governments', which is inconsistent with the $21bn figure; official phase-1 registered capital was 138.7 bn yuan (CLM-0132).

claim: AMD completed its 'Asset Smart' transaction with ATIC and Mubadala in early 2009, creating GLOBALFOUNDRIES, which AMD consolidated in its results as of March 2, 2009.
evidence: "AMD completed its Asset Smart transaction with the Advanced Technology Investment Company (ATIC) and Mubadala Development Company of Abu Dhabi, creating GLOBALFOUNDRIES"; "AMD consolidates the operating results of GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. in its results as of March 2, 2009" (AMD Q1 2009 release, Ex. 99.1, Apr 21, 2009)
notes: Fact-check fc-W0-b17b: primary support for the 'later GlobalFoundries' part of CLM-0112, which SRC-0064 (Oct 2008) does not contain.
